paper.title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: A programmatic (Pythonic) LLM prompt structure - imported action primitives, a list of environment objects, example programs with natural-language comments and assert-based state checks with recovery actions - lets an LLM generate executable, situated task plans that work across environments, robot capabilities and tasks; the authors claim state-of-the-art success on VirtualHome household tasks and deployment on a physical robot arm for tabletop tasks.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope: frozen LLM planner driving a simulated household agent and a real Franka arm through executable primitive calls (A-type harness).

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; central support is VH Env-0 10 tasks x 5 runs (SR 0.34 GPT3 vs 0.00 re-implemented Huang et al.), 2x2 comments/feedback ablation with GPT3 fixed; assertion feedback reads the ground-truth state graph via an LLM; Env-1/2 scene results without baselines; robot results are 9 single runs without assertions that the authors call qualitative; no cost. Expected evidence_level online, claim_support scoped.

evidence.quote: We present a programmatic LLM prompt structure that enables plan generation functional across situated environments, robot capabilities, and tasks. Our key insight is to prompt the LLM with program-like specifications of the available actions and objects in an environment, as well as with example programs that can be executed. We make concrete recommendations about prompt structure and generation constraints through ablation experiments, demonstrate state of the art success rates in Vir
evidence.support_explanation: Author's broad portability claim and concrete prompting intervention.

evidence.quote: Plan functions consist of API calls to action primitives, comments to summarize actions, and assertions for tracking execution
evidence.support_explanation: Executable plan interface, comments and assertions are distinct operations.

Each environment contains 115 unique object instances (Fig. 2 ), including class-level duplicates. Each object has properties corresponding to its action affordances. Some objects also have a semantic state

SR is the fraction of executions that achieved all task-relevant goal-conditions. Exec is the fraction of actions in the plan that are executable in the environment, even if they are not relevant for the task. GCR is measured using the set difference between ground truth final state conditions \mathbf{g} and the final state achieved \mathbf{g}^{\prime} with the generated plan, divided by the number of task-specific goal-conditions; SR =1 only if GCR =1 .

signatures.object: The planner prompt: Pythonic header with imported action primitives, an environment object list, three fixed example plan programs with NL comments; the LLM (GPT-3 / Codex / Davinci) completes the next task function.
signatures.information: Sees the action list, the object list (global list of all VirtualHome object instances in the scene; detector output on the real robot) and example programs; does not see the goal state or any state feedback while generating.
signatures.operation: Few-shot code completion of a plan program (API calls over objects plus comments), interpreted step by step by the simulator / robot.
signatures.output: Executable plan function; Exec = share of actions executable.
signatures.conditions: Same primitives as imported; 3 fixed examples (2 for Davinci); object list local per plan on the robot.
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: single sampled program per task; backbone (GPT3 vs Codex vs Davinci) and example count compared on the same reported setting.
signatures.persistence: not_applicable: no state kept between tasks; no retained improvement claimed.
signatures.claimed_effect: VirtualHome SR 0.34 / Exec 0.84 / GCR 0.65 (GPT3) vs 0.00 / 0.45 / 0.21 for the re-implemented baseline of [2].
signatures.failure_boundary: Scene-agnostic prompt; environment artifacts; plans cut by API caps; ambiguous tasks; single final-state scoring.

signatures.object: Execution-time assert statements with LLM-judged state checks and recovery actions embedded in the generated program.
signatures.information: VirtualHome state graph (symbolic, object properties and relations) passed to an LLM that answers whether the assertion holds; unavailable on the real robot.
signatures.operation: Before an action, check a precondition; if false run the recovery branch (e.g. find) already written in the plan.
signatures.output: Closed-loop corrected execution inside the plan program.
signatures.conditions: Only simulation; recovery branches must be anticipated by the LLM; no general action-success feedback.
signatures.feedback: LLM judgement of assertion over symbolic state
signatures.claimed_effect: Feedback ablation (rows 3 vs 4, 5 vs 6) improves metrics; SR 0.34 vs 0.28 with comments, 0.30 vs 0.18 without.
signatures.failure_boundary: Generated assertions do not cover all cases; assertion judge is an unaudited LLM.

gap.author_gap: Scoring-style LLM planners need all next steps enumerated; text-generation planners emit actions/objects that do not map to the robot or scene; environment state feedback is missing in LLM task planning.
gap.checked_gap: Real and sourced: the cited neighbours (Huang et al. [2] open-loop with action matching; SayCan enumerate-and-score; InnerMonologue feedback but off-scene objects) each leave the stated residue. Importance for the embodied setting is plausible but only quantified against one neighbour.
lineage: Huang et al. zero-shot planners [2] (open-loop, 1 retrieved example) -> SayCan [4] (affordance-weighted scoring) / InnerMonologue [1] (feedback, still off-scene objects) -> concurrent Socratic Models [3] (code completion) -> ProgPrompt (imports + object list + comments + asserts)
gap.closest_adjacent: InnerMonologue and Socratic Models are the closest (feedback, code completion) but are not empirically compared; only [2] is re-implemented.
gap.residue: Plans that name unavailable actions/objects and never check preconditions against the current state.
gap.stakes: Executability on a given robot and scene (Exec 0.45 for the baseline).
gap.method_response: Pythonic imports and object list narrow the output space; example programs show structure; comments act as chain-of-thought; assertions check preconditions with recovery.
gap.remaining_gap: Strict-goal scoring, ambiguous tasks, no action-success feedback, scene-specific affordances, asserts not exercised on the robot, SR still 0.34.
gap.current_relevance: Later work 2302.01560 (same batch) re-implements ProgPrompt in Minecraft and reports an average success of 16.88 vs 15.42 for a plain zero-shot planner (author re-implementation), suggesting the program format alone transfers weakly to long-horizon open worlds; not used to lower the score.
unresolved: No quantitative comparison with SayCan, InnerMonologue or Socratic Models; closest-neighbour judgement rests on the paper's own related-work text and local pinned sources only.
Independent attribution of program schema vs extra contextual knowledge (imports/object list never toggled).
gap.aggregate_note: Sol's checked gap retained: programmatic constraints address feasibility failures but not uncertain physical execution or correctness of symbolic preconditions (sol checked_gap). G=3 agreed.

claims.setting: Franka Panda, pick-and-place primitive, ViLD object list, 4 tasks, 9 single-run rows
claims.result_denominator: 9 single-run rows over 4 tasks: executed SR 7/9, Plan SR 8/9 (counterfactual); assertions off
counterevidence: gripper slip and soup-can/bottle confusion failures
claims.allowed_conclusion: A feasibility demonstration of text-to-plan grounding on one arm with a given pick-and-place policy; not a measured success rate.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop VirtualHome goal-condition success with repeated runs; robot results are qualitative single runs without assertions; Env-1/2 scene results use the privileged ground-truth state graph and object list (anchor precedent 1). No transfer.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: A programmatic (Pythonic) LLM prompt structure - imported action primitives, a list of environment objects, example programs with natural-language comments and assert-based state checks with recovery actions - lets an LLM generate executable, situated task plans that work across environments, robot capabilities and tasks; the authors claim state-of-the-art success on VirtualHome household tasks and deployment on a physical robot arm for tabletop tasks.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With GPT-3 and three fixed program examples, the Pythonic prompt (imports, object list, comments, asserts over the simulator state graph) yields far more executable plans than a re-implemented open-loop language baseline in VirtualHome (SR 0.34 vs 0.00, Exec 0.84 vs 0.45, 10 tasks x 5 runs, one scene); comments help consistently, the assertion benefit is directional; the format can drive a Franka arm through a given pick-and-place policy in 9 single-run configurations. State-of-the-art over SayCan/Inner Monologue and broad generalisation are not established.
unresolved: no comparison with SayCan / Inner Monologue / Socratic Models
assessment.reproduction: author_report only; no reproduction by us

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Concrete, sourced bottleneck (enumerate-and-score cost; free text naming unavailable actions/objects; missing state feedback) with named neighbours (Huang et al., SayCan, Inner Monologue, Socratic). Not 4: only the open-loop Huang baseline is run, so the residual relative to feedback-based neighbours is argued, not measured.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Imports/object list narrow output, comments act as stepwise guidance, asserts check preconditions; a reconstructable mechanism with testable predictions (comments/feedback toggles). Weak points: assertion judge is an unaudited LLM over the state graph; imports/object list never toggled.

X.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Prompt construction, interpreter execution and assertion flow can be rebuilt; failure boundaries discussed in V-B. Not 4: the robot instantiation drops assertions, and the LLM-judge prompt and recovery generation are thin.

measurement.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed under anchors v2. Simulator goal-condition SR with 10 tasks x 5 runs, but single-reference-goal scoring mislabels valid alternatives (conceded), only 10 of the 70-task set are reported, and the robot evidence is 9 single-run rows with a counterfactual Plan SR.

causality.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). The 2x2 comments x feedback grid with GPT3 fixed is real component evidence, but the headline gain (program prompt vs language prompting) is confounded: Huang et al. gets 1 dynamic example vs 3 fixed, LangPrompt needs an extra GPT2 mapper, imports/object list are never toggled, and the feedback delta (0.34+-0.08 vs 0.28+-0.04) sits within about 1 sd. Anchor 2: key gain has unseparated confounds.

holdout.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Prompt-count selection on VH, two extra scenes (SR 0.56) without baselines, robot rows without assertions; no contamination discussion.

statistics.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). Five LLM-sampling runs with sd and a per-task table exist, but there is no CI or paired test, failures are only qualitative, the key feedback ablation difference lies within about 1 sd unaddressed, and the robot half of the claim has no repeats. Anchor v2: variance present but no CI and no failure decomposition -> 2, not 3.

cost.reason: Both seats not_reported/0; confirmed. No call, token, latency or dollar figures; assertions add uncounted LLM calls; only a Codex rate-limit remark.
search_scope: full pinned text Abstract-VI incl. Tables I-IV captions (no appendix exists)

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE transfer needs closed-loop success on an embodiment/scene set unused in construction or >=2 embodiments with closed-loop success. Robot route: 9 single-run rows (agg:E001), assertions disabled, Plan SR counterfactual and the authors themselves frame the physical results as a qualitative demonstration (son55:E021); the plans are open-loop at the planner level. Treating this as counted cross-embodiment transfer would rely on a demonstration, which EVIDENCE rule 1 excludes. Scene route (Env-1/Env-2): the harness reads the simulator's ground-truth state graph and global object list (agg:E003), a privileged channel; anchor precedent 1 bars transfer under privileged simulator symbolic state. son55 itself flagged the call as borderline.
resolutions.score_impact: none (evidence_level is not scored); affects transfer-label eligibility only

resolutions.reason: Few-shot conditioning is shared with the main comparator (Huang et al. is also in-context prompting), so it is not the operation that differentiates the paper. The differentiating move is the C25 signature: emit a typed executable program over imported primitives, run it in an interpreter, and close the loop mid-execution with assertion checks (sol:E002, son55:E009). Conditioning is kept as a supporting operation because swapping the import/object lists to adapt to new scenes/agents is a distinct, claimed operation.

C03's tactic requires an upstream phase teaching the model to parse the schema or a reference substrate transferred through a learned shared space; ProgPrompt has three fixed hand-written examples and no upstream or retrieval step (son55 itself marked step 3 absent). The parent operation (task and robot capabilities expressed as conditioning, solved without parameter updates) applies, so supporting=adapt_via_conditioning with sub_id null. C25 is the only child of decompose_and_delegate and its steps 1-4 are executed (step 3 via LLM-judged assertions, partial).

K105 agreed (structural: plan program composes primitives; no persistent coding runtime). K104 fits: the imported action vocabulary is executed by the VH interpreter / a pick-and-place policy (son55:E007). K201 rejected: its checker must sit outside the model and not use the evaluation oracle, whereas ProgPrompt's assertions are generated by the planner and judged by an LLM over the ground-truth state graph (agg:E003); recorded as unassigned with son55's revision proposal kept pending.
See rating reason: headline comparison confounded by example budget (1 vs 3) and an extra GPT2 mapper; imports/object list never toggled; feedback delta within noise.
Anchor v2 statistics band: repeats with sd but no CI/paired test and no counted failure decomposition; robot half unrepeated.
Same backbone is used, but the alternative harness is denied the same example budget and uses a different action mapper.

The paper discloses that the example count was selected by evaluating on VH (sol:E004), which lets a reader see the overlap, but does not say which tasks and does not discuss pretraining exposure: partial disclosure, not absent.
Final display uses python round(raw,1) on raw 61.25 -> 61.2; son55 used round-half-up. Raw is authoritative for selection.
